subject: Stream SLO + Dedicated Capacity: GPU matrix & validation plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Nguyen <alyssa@quantumledger.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Stream SLO + Dedicated Capacity: GPU matrix & validation plan

Hi Alyssa — great to meet you and the QuantumLedger team today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance/SLOs and next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity and run a validation pass.

Key items we captured on the call:
- Primary flow: low-latency chat with streaming token delivery to client (chunked SSE/HTTP streaming).
- Target SLOs: interactive chat with p95 token latency goal of <= 120 ms, p99 tail under ~350 ms for standard prompts.
- Throughput/Concurrency: steady-state ~300 requests/sec with typical prompts (avg 120 tokens), peak bursts up to ~2k rps during batch job windows. Concurrent active sessions estimated at 60–90.
- Streaming requirements: progressive token flushing, ability to stop/restart streams without re-running entire prompt.
- Data: no PII-heavy payloads; logs/audit required for enterprise compliance.

Attached is a lightweight SLO sizing matrix (slo-sizing-matrix.xlsx) and our benchmark summary PDF — will help us pick GPU family and reserved throughput.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the p95/p99 targets above and any extremes we should include (e.g., large-context prompts 8k tokens).
2) Our SE (Karthik) will draft a Dedicated sizing matrix (GPU options + throughput targets) and propose a 48-hour validation window to run against your staging traffic pattern.
3) We'll schedule the validation window; after the run we’ll deliver run artifacts and a recommendation (H100 vs A100 or mixed pool) for the initial Dedicated commit.

Are you ok with that plan? If so, would you prefer us to validate against a snapshot of production traffic or a synthetic workload?

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor

From: Alyssa Nguyen <alyssa@quantumledger.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, DevOps Team <devops@quantumledger.ai>
Date: 2026-10-24T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stream SLO + Dedicated Capacity: GPU matrix & validation plan

Thanks Grace — good recap. Confirming details and adding a few clarifications from our side:

Confirmed SLOs:
- p50 token latency: ~25–40 ms (we target snappy feel).
- p95 token latency: <= 120 ms (hard requirement for chat).
- p99 token latency: ideally < 350 ms; for long-context (>4k tokens) we can tolerate up to 500 ms.

Throughput/Concurrency:
- Typical: 250–350 RPS (mostly 1–2 request bursts per user).
- Peak: we see spikes up to 1.8k RPS during end-of-day reconciliation windows.
- Concurrent sessions: average 70 active; planning for headroom to 120.

Streaming specifics:
- We use SSE with incremental JSON chunks; we need low first-byte latency and steady token cadence.
- Clients may cancel mid-stream frequently; ability to resume is +nice-to-have but not blocking.

Model footprint / prompts:
- Average prompt+context per session: ~420 tokens. Max context we'll test: 8k.
- We are OK with 8-bit quantized variants if latency/throughput tradeoffs are favorable.

Validation preference:
- We'd prefer Redwood to validate against a captured staging trace (sanitized) to reproduce request shapes and pause/resume behavior.
- We can provide a 48-hour window next week (UTC-friendly) and a Slack channel for live troubleshooting.

Attached a brief CSV with our typical request-size distribution and a short doc listing streaming expectations.

Best,
Alyssa Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantumLedger
alyssa@quantumledger.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Dedicated sizing recommendation for QuantumLedger (draft)

Quick internal note after Alyssa's confirmation — proposed sizing options and validation scope.

Assumptions pulled from Alyssa's data: avg 420 tokens/session, steady 300 RPS, peaks 1.8k RPS, concurrent headroom 120, streaming + resume/cancel behavior.

Sizing options (initial recommendation):
- Option A (Performance-first): 6x NVIDIA H100-80GB nodes, reserved throughput ~45k tokens/sec sustained, burst to 120k tokens/sec; expected p95 token latency ~60–100 ms. Good for low tail latency and long-context.
- Option B (Cost-balanced): 8x NVIDIA A100-80GB nodes, reserved throughput ~40k tokens/sec sustained, burst to 90k tokens/sec; expected p95 token latency ~90–140 ms for quantized int8 models.
- Option C (Mixed pool + fallback): 4x H100 + 6x A100, routing policy: latency-critical requests -> H100; background/batch -> A100. Reserved throughput split 60/40 H100/A100.

Validation plan (48 hours):
- Run a captured staging trace (sanitized) with realistic interleaving and cancel patterns.
- Metrics to capture: token p50/p95/p99 latencies, first-byte time, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, mem pressure, KV cache hit ratio.
- Deliverables: raw traces, aggregated dashboards, recommended commit size + fallback policy, cost estimate delta for each option.

Attachments I will prepare for Alyssa: gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf and a small XLSX that maps request shapes to expected tokens/sec and GPU utilization.

If no objections I'll send this draft to Alyssa with a proposed validation window: Nov 2–3 (UTC-friendly).

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments: gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf (internal), slo-sizing-matrix.xlsx (draft)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Stream SLO + Dedicated Capacity: GPU matrix & validation plan

Alyssa — thanks for the quick confirmation and for sharing the distribution CSV. All looks good on our side. Proposed next steps and asks:

1) Validation window: Nov 2–3 (48 hours). Please confirm whether that slot works for your team. We will need the sanitized staging trace by EOD Nov 1.
2) We plan to run Option A and Option B profiles against the trace (H100 and A100 variants) and produce the artifacts Karthik described. Option C (mixed) will be evaluated if Option B fails to meet p95 on streaming workloads.
3) Access: please add our account (validation@redwood.com) to the staging bucket with the trace file and share a Slack channel.
4) Deliverables: run dashboard link, a PDF run summary (gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf), and recommended Dedicated commit + fallback routing.

If that all sounds right, can you confirm the window and share the trace link (Drive or S3) and a contact for the staging environment? Once confirmed we'll put calendar invites on the books and share the validation playbook.

Thanks — excited to get this validated and convert to a Dedicated commit that meets your latency goals.

Grace
